summary: Peter Kuhlmann works in linguistics and other fields. He completed his doctoral studies under Rosemarie Lühr (~1989–1993) and held posts at the University of Giessen (~1996–2002), Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (~2002–2004), and the University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter M. Scharf specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, and held posts at Brown University (attested 2000, 2006–2009), the Sanskrit Library (attested 2014, 2024–2025), and IIIT Hyderabad.
Peter Masefield is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and doctoral supervisor Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, alongside several academic and traditional teachers.

Peter N. Gregory specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning his Ph.D. at Harvard University in 1981 under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held positions at the Kuroda Institute, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Smith College.

Peter Peterson was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh under Theodor Aufrecht and at Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College (~1873–1899) and Fellow and Registrar at the University of Mumbai (~1881–1899).

Peter Schreiner works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Münster under Paul Hacker and habilitated at the University of Tübingen, later holding posts at Tübingen (1974–1982), SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an M.A. at the University of Washington in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his doctorate (~1976–1982) and Habilitation (~1982–1995) at the University of Bonn. He held positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences (1978), Humboldt University of Berlin (2001), and the University of Bonn (2001).

Peter Skilling specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the École Pratique des Hautes Études by 2004. He has held positions at Chulalongkorn University, École française d'Extrême-Orient, and the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation, which he founded.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Clare College, Cambridge. His career includes posts at Cambridge, the University of Reading, the Courtauld Institute of Art, and the University of Oxford and its Classical Art Research Centre.

Peter Zieme specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin, he held posts at the Institut für Orientforschung, the GDR Academy of Sciences, BBAW, and the Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer works in religious studies, Indology, and sinology. After studying at Groningen and Utrecht, he held posts at Utrecht University, the University of Amsterdam, the University of Pennsylvania, and served as Director at the MPI-MMG (~2008–2021).

Peter von Bohlen studied at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under scholars including August Wilhelm von Schlegel, Georg Freytag, and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1825 until his death.

Peter von Bradke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tartu, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Jena, Leipzig, and Giessen, where he completed his Habilitation and served as professor from 1886 to 1896.

Peter von Köppen worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (~1809–1814) and the University of Tübingen (~1819–1821), and later held a post at the Ministry of State Property.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Heinz Bechert (~1980–1989) and has held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (~2003), and the Pali Text Society (~2003).

Petra Maurer works in Tibetology and Indology, having studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held affiliations with the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the University of Munich, IKGF Erlangen, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Dzongsar Institute (~1998–2004) and under several traditional masters, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (both attested 2017).
